notes:
Summary: Halcyon Ledger is a mid-tier global asset manager trying to replace an aging keyword search for research analysts. Primary driver: reduce time-to-insight for traders and PMs while meeting strict residency and KMS controls. They want a RAG-style search where dense embeddings + fast ANN find candidates and a token-efficient reranker (distilled cross-encoder) reorders top-k. Preferences: dedicated capacity for predictable p99 SLA and private control plane (VPC).

Highlights / rep notes:
- "We cannot hand over master keys; BYOK + HSM-backed KMS required." said Head of Security on 10/7.
- Indexing scale: target 30–80M documents (research notes, 10 years retention), estimate ~2–6 TB vector footprint depending on quantization. Need autoscale for end-of-month ingestion spikes.
- Latency targets: median end-to-end lookup+rerank ~150–300ms; p95 < 500ms for analyst queries. Query volume: 8k–18k QPS/day, peaks trading-hours.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement target cost_per_query < $0.03 for typical search (ANN + lightweight rerank) — will trade some cost for guaranteed latency.
- Model preferences: open/quantized encoders for embeddings; reranker can be smaller cross-encoder hosted on dedicated GPUs. Want Redwood to recommend quantization profile and batching config (Optimize).

POC specifics and asks:
- Run a 7-day perf run on Dedicated with BYOK KMS in NA region; test with 5M -> 50M index slices. Measure token-level cost, latency breakdown (search vs rerank), and cache hit impact.
- Security: provide written KMS key lifecycle, support for HSM-backed keys, SOC2 attestation, and data residency SLA.
- Legal: need a security addendum (Governing law: NY) and a CAIQ-lite + penetration test summary.

Stated blockers: KMS escrow policy (legal), definitive residency proof for specific EU/NA segmentation later in rollout, PO release timing.

Next steps assigned: Marcus to deliver updated SOW by 2025-11-07; Priya to schedule 7-day perf window starting 2025-11-10 (engineer patch and monitoring hooks), Kenji to track procurement approvals.

Freeform snippets from calls: "We need deterministic latency; any dynamic batching that spikes p99 is a non-starter." — Head of Research.
